result.summary: Encapsulates CScriptWitness and replaces its internal std::vector of element vectors with a single allocation containing serialized witness data. Individual witness elements are parsed on the fly rather than stored as separate vector allocations, making witness objects immutable once constructed. Accessors, iteration, and serialization across the codebase are converted to use the new encapsulated interface.
result.problem: Transactions with many small witness elements create an allocation and a 24-byte vector overhead for every non-empty element, allowing specially crafted transactions to consume excessive memory after deserialization (up to roughly 28 bytes per weight unit in the worst case).
evidence: Worst-case allocated size for transactions kept in memory drops from roughly 28 bytes/WU to 1.6 bytes/WU (PR description).
CScriptWitness shrinks from 24 to 8 bytes, and CTxIn from 112 to 96 bytes (PR description).
Issue reported by furszy and 0xB10C (PR description).
Tradeoff acknowledged by author: 'worsens deserialization and validation time, adding some 50-70 ms per block to the worst case for me' (PR description).
result.scope_notes: Contains four scripted-diff commits that mechanically convert direct `.stack` access across dozens of files before changing the underlying storage layout.
result.card: This pull request refactors CScriptWitness from storing an array of byte vectors into a single buffer holding serialized witness data. This resolves a memory amplification vulnerability where transactions with millions of tiny witness elements consume up to 28 bytes per weight unit in memory, dropping the worst-case footprint to 1.6 bytes per weight unit. Accessing elements becomes an on-the-fly deserialization operation, which adds roughly 50 to 70 ms per block in worst-case validation time. It spans 62 files, largely via mechanical scripted diffs that migrate callers to encapsulated accessors.

risk.why: A flaw in witness serialization, deserialization, or element indexing could corrupt the execution stack passed to Script evaluation, leading to consensus divergence or validation crashes.
